title: Blend AI & Weight Map
prompt:
PAGE 3 & PAGE 4: Blend AI Explorer & Spatial Weight Map Engine.
Deep-dive into the AI-NWP hybrid forecast fusion mechanism:

1. Weight Mode Switcher (5 selectable operational modes):
   - Equal-weight baseline (1/N uniform)
   - Historical skill (climatology & rolling 30-day verification)
   - Context-aware neural gating (PyTorch regime-conditioned weighting)
   - Bayesian / BMA comparison (predictive distribution mixture)
   - Hybrid production blend [ACTIVE]

2. Production Formula Interactive Simulator:
   - Formula display: W_final = α·W_neural + β·W_skill + γ·W_equal
   - Sliders with real-time numeric readouts:
     * α (Neural weight): 0.55
     * β (Skill weight): 0.35
     * γ (Equal baseline): 0.10
   - Constraint badge: 'Convex combination: Σ weights = 1.00, non-negative, physically bounded'.

3. Model Stacked Contribution over Lead Time (+6h to +240h):
   - Stacked visual breakdown showing AI models (GraphCast, AIFS) dominating short-medium lead (+6h to +96h) and physical NWP models (NCUM-G, NEPS-G ensemble) retaining higher weight at +120h to +240h for deep atmospheric conservation.

4. Spatial Weight Contribution Map (One model at a time):
   - Active model chip selector: [GraphCast (38% avg)] | [NCUM-G (32% avg)] | [BharatFS (16% avg)] | [AIFS (14% avg)]
   - Indian map heat representation in grey-to-sand ramp with readouts: Min: 0.04 (Himalayan complex terrain), Max: 0.62 (Peninsular maritime plains), Mean: 0.28.
   - Side panel 'Why this weight?': Top feature drivers:
     1. Terrain complexity (Western Ghats & Himalayas penalize pure neural grids, favors BharatFS/NCUM-G)
     2. Monsoon active regime (favors coupled physics)
     3. Coastal distance (sea-breeze front adjustment)
     4. Ensemble spread agreement index.

5. Lead-Time Scrubber: 0h to 240h in 6-hour steps with play/pause and valid UTC timestamp.
